en: Points of Controversy:
The Chapter on Latent Dispositions,
Eleventh Section.
In a discourse on knowledge:
When a consciousness that is devoid of knowledge and dissociated from knowledge is occurring, should it not be said that "it possesses knowledge"?
“Yes.
“When lust has vanished, should it not be said that one is ‘free from lust’?”
It should not be said so ...
[and so on] ... when ignorance has disappeared and a consciousness dissociated from knowledge is occurring, should it not be said that one "possesses knowledge"?
“Yes,” he replied.
“When hatred has vanished… when delusion has vanished…”
When defilements have vanished, should it not be said that one is "free from defilements"? It should not be said so... [and so forth].
When passion has vanished, should it be said that one is "free from passion"? Yes.
When ignorance has ceased and a consciousness dissociated from knowledge is occurring, should it be said that "one possesses knowledge"?
One should not say so …pe…
When hatred has vanished… when delusion has vanished… when the defilements have vanished, it should be said:
“Is one ‘free from defilement’? Yes.
When ignorance has vanished and a consciousness dissociated from knowledge is occurring, should it be said: [that one is free from defilement]?

“Is one ‘possessing knowledge’? One should not say so… [and so on]… When ignorance has vanished and a consciousness dissociated from knowledge is occurring, it should be said: [that one is not possessing knowledge].
“Is he a possessor of knowledge?”—
Yes, he is.
Is he a possessor of knowledge by means of past knowledge— by knowledge that has ceased, vanished, and subsided?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … The Discussion on Knowledge is finished.
